faq.a: Sahar is associated with the Arabic form سَحَر, whose core sense is sahar; dawn, daybreak.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sahar?
faq.a: Sahar is associated with Arabic. Sahar is Arabic سَحَر (Saḥar), meaning 'dawn, the time before daybreak'.
Yes — the underlying form سَحَر is Arabic.
Sahar can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sahar should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س ح ر is Quranic, but Saḥar is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sahar mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sahar is rendered سحر and carries the sense سحر، صبح.

faq.q: What does Sahar mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sahar is rendered سحر and carries the sense سحر، سپیده‌دم.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-har. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sahar?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sahar, sahar. Script forms are سحر, سَحَر, सहर.

faq.q: Is Sahar a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
